title: Toxic English Version Hits Indian Screens Today With Tighter 18-Minute Shorter Cut
excerpt: The English version of Yash's pan-India gangster drama arrives in Indian cinemas on September 4 with a leaner runtime, even as the film's box office trajectory remains a talking point after a sharp post-opening decline.
body:
• The English version of Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups releases in Indian cinemas on September 4, running 18 minutes shorter than the Indian-language versions at 2 hours and 57 minutes.
  • The film was simultaneously shot in Kannada and English, making the English cut an original version rather than a dub.
  • Lionsgate holds international English distribution rights, while the Indian-language versions are distributed overseas by Phars Film.
  • The release comes as Toxic's box office performance has fallen short of expectations following a Rs 140 crore worldwide opening day.

The English version of Yash's gangster drama Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups arrives in Indian cinemas today, September 4, offering audiences a tighter cut of the film that runs 18 minutes shorter than its Indian-language counterparts.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=alOy_d-_c8g

Director Geetu Mohandas confirmed the release on social media, describing the English version as "one of the languages the film was written and shot in" with "a shorter cut from the Indian language version." The English version clocks in at 2 hours and 57 minutes, compared to 3 hours and 14 minutes for the Kannada, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, and Malayalam versions.

A Rare Simultaneous English Production

Toxic stands as a rare pan-India film that was produced in six languages, including English, from inception. Unlike most Indian films that receive dubbed English versions after the fact, the English cut of Toxic was shot simultaneously alongside the Kannada version, making it an original production rather than a translation.

https://x.com/KvnProductions/status/2095406175026295070

The Central Board of Film Certification granted the English version an 'A' certificate on September 1. The film will screen across major Indian cities including Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Kochi, and Thiruvananthapuram.

Split International Distribution

The distribution strategy reflects the film's ambition to reach beyond traditional Indian cinema audiences. Phars Film acquired international theatrical rights exclusively for the five Indian-language versions, while Lionsgate secured the English distribution across international territories — targeting mainstream, non-diaspora audiences and wider western theatrical chains.

The English version already released overseas on August 26, the same day the Indian-language versions opened both domestically and internationally. The delayed Indian release of the English cut marks an unusual staggered rollout within the home market.

Box Office Context

The English release arrives at a challenging moment for the film's commercial trajectory. Toxic opened to a massive Rs 140 crore worldwide on its first day, driven by enormous anticipation for Yash's return after the blockbuster KGF Chapter 2. However, collections dropped sharply on day two and slipped into single digits within the first week, according to industry tracking.

"Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups, in English — one of the languages the film was written and shot in. A shorter cut from the Indian language version."

— Geetu Mohandas, Director

Mixed reviews and polarized audience reactions have weighed on the film's theatrical momentum. By the end of its first week, Toxic's cumulative performance fell well below expectations given its scale, star power, and reported production investment.

The English version's tighter runtime could appeal to viewers who found the original cut overlong. The film also faces stiff competition today from Mirzapur: The Movie and Arshad Warsi's Jeevan Ya Bheema Con?, both releasing on the same date.

Toxic stars Yash in a double role alongside Nayanthara, Kiara Advani, Huma Qureshi, Tara Sutaria, Rukmini Vasanth, and Akshay Oberoi. The film is produced by Venkat K Narayana's KVN Productions and Yash's Monster Mind Creations.
